messages.subject: Meeting this Wednesday
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies,

Welcome back from Spring Break! We are meeting at our normal time this Wednesday (4/3): 10am-noon in the Datalab classroom (360 Shields library). This meeting is to help folks who come in with R programming questions, so come join us and we'll figure out how to help you. This is a hybrid meeting so you can also join us via Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!
The message I'm forwarding here lists the workshops that will be taught in Datalab this quarter. We're teaching about databases! We're teaching about machine learning! We're teaching about language models! We're teaching about models for categorical data! The workshops begin this Thursday with the first session about databases.

Registration is free. Please join us!
-Wes

messages.subject: Meeting Tomorrow 10-12 and R Help File mini-workshop next week
messages.subject_clean: Meeting Tomorrow 10-12 and R Help File mini-workshop next week
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

Join us tomorrow at our typical meeting time, 10-noon in the Datalab classroom (360 Shields library). It is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. This is a hybrid meeting so you can also join us via Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Also next week we will be having a mini-workshop on reading R help files <https://d-rug.github.io/help_file_anatomy/>! It's great that R has a ton of built in documentation, but that documentation is only helpful if you can actually read it. Unfortunately it is frequently written for people who already know what they are doing, and are familiar with words like "argument" and "method". This workshop will help you translate "r-speak" into English. Snacks will be provided.

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators
